provenance.author: pilot writer (Claude Opus 5.5, model-written)
notes: Bootstrap chapter (design §2.1 exemption): map exposition with contrasts inside newly established material; no characters yet.

(Pilot, 2026-10-12; superseded by the gentle-opening pass below.) Running words 390, below the advisory 405–495 window. With 32 lexemes and only G01 grammar, every further sentence I tried restated a map fact; the design forbids padding (§2.1, editorial-decisions). Names and map carry the rest.

(Pilot; at 390 words.) Gloss density is above the Rhan 1 band (about 5 per 100 words) because nearly every predicative adjective and noun in a zero-knowledge chapter is a new, mutated word that §2.3(a) requires to be glossed. Second occurrences inside the same sentence share one gloss.
No 'A ti?' item: second-person forms arrive in Pennod 5; Pensum C ends with a small production item (c7) instead.

Predicative yn contracts to 'n after a vowel (Cymru'n wlad); locative yn never contracts (Cymru yn Ynys Prydain). The wrong accepted answer 'Mae Cymru'n Ynys Prydain' was removed from C/c1 after model review; note the answer normaliser still expands every 'n to yn, so a lint for locative 'n is recommended.

Gentle-opening pass 2026-10-19 (owner, learning from the course, found Pennod 1 a bit too hard): 524 running words (was 390), 86 sentences (was 63), the same 32 new lexemes, so one new item per 16.4 words (was 12.2). Re-paced opening: the locative block s005–s010 now comes before s004, so the reader meets about 60 words of Dyma / ar / yn (in) / ble / hefyd before the first predicative yn and mutation; mawr appears unmutated (s066 môr mawr) before fawr, tywyll (s080) before dywyll, and trefi before the glossed predicative dref (s076). Added material: more on Iwerddon (Ewrop, size, the sea), Cymru between Iwerddon and Lloegr, mountains in the Alban, Ynys Môn, Afon Wysg only in Cymru, Caerfyrddin, Llundain, the dark mountains round the cwm, Hafren against Afon Helyg, bryn against mynyddoedd (gloss bryn = mynydd bach), the cave high on the hill, the long hall, and where the forest lies. Existing text changed only to match the pictures: s048 (the river does not run through the forest; this also removes the two-yn clause queried earlier), s054 (the river, not the llys, lies between the llys and the hill; Gramadeg row and Pensum C c5 follow), s057 (tai bach reads as toilets; now tai, with their smallness in s084). Map: labels Ynys Môn, Caerfyrddin, Llundain; three small peaks round Cwm Helyg so that s041 rhwng y mynyddoedd is true on the map. Stopped at 524 running words rather than the 650–750 aim: two independent reviews (Codex gpt-6-astra; a separate Claude Opus critic) agreed that further sentences with this vocabulary and grammar would restate map facts (design §1.1, §6.2), and that the gain in ease comes from the ramp rather than the total.

Audit-fix pass 2026-10-19 (docs/reviews/welsh-russian-lessons-2026-10-19.md; the gentle-opening re-pacing is untouched, no story text changed): Pensum A no longer tests the noun–adjective gender mutation this chapter defers (old a7 'tŷ ___ (mawr)', now 'yn ___ (tref) → dref'); the trivial no-change items a2/a4 (answer = cue) are now two-gap items that set an unchanged adjective beside a mutated one (hir | fach, uchel | fawr); a6 no longer copies s028 (now 'Mae'r bryn yn fynydd bach', the bryn gloss). Pensum B: b8 no longer needs 'gwlad + bach → gwlad fach' (now wrth); b7 accepted two bank words (hir/fawr) and needed the feminine mutation, now a predicative contrast with one answer (fawr); b5's dialogue no longer gives away b8. Pensum C c1/c4/c6 accept more correct answers (both Ewrop and Ynys Prydain; 'yn uchel ar y bryn'; 'yn y cwm'). Meta-language: 'dim newid' (dim is Pennod 6, newid never taught) replaced by arrows (ll → ll, rh → rh; hir → hir). Gloss: 'mynydd, mynyddoedd' gave form only; now 'mynydd ▲, mynyddoedd ▲▲', the map's mountain sign. Filled the unfilled {WORDS} placeholder in the gentle-opening note (524).

cover.alt: Map of the island of Britain: Wales, England and Scotland; Ireland across the sea to the west and Brittany across the sea to the south. London is marked in England. An enlarged inset of Wales shows the island of Anglesey, the mountains of Eryri, the rivers Hafren and Wysg, the city of Caerllion, the town of Carmarthen, and a tiny dot for Cwm Helyg among three small peaks.
cover.art_brief: Hand-authored SVG map, reused in Penodau 13, 23 and 36. Island of Britain with internal borders for Cymru, Lloegr and Yr Alban; Iwerddon to the west and Llydaw to the south, both across the sea, with a hint of the European mainland in the lower right corner labelled Ewrop. A city dot for Llundain in south-east England. Mountain symbols in Eryri with Yr Wyddfa marked, and one small mountain in northern England; Ynys Môn labelled off Eryri; the river Hafren drawn long through Wales and England; the river Wysg in south-east Wales with a walled-city symbol for Caerllion on it; a town dot for Caerfyrddin in the south-west; a very small dot in south Wales labelled Cwm Helyg, with three small peaks round it. Sea in pale blue-grey with the label 'y môr'. Welsh labels only, at least 14 px: Ynys Prydain, Cymru, Lloegr, Yr Alban, Iwerddon, Llydaw, Ewrop, Llundain, Eryri, Yr Wyddfa, Ynys Môn, Hafren, Wysg, Caerllion, Caerfyrddin, Cwm Helyg, y môr. viewBox, <title> and <desc>; no raster.

grammar.nodyn_en: Mae means 'is' or 'there is'. Yn has two jobs. Before a place it means 'in' (yn Ewrop; yng Nghymru is a fixed chunk for now). Before a describing word or noun it links it to the subject and softens the first letter: mawr → yn fawr, dinas → yn ddinas. Ll- and rh- stay unchanged.
